content.text:
I wrote the migrated file to `out/module.ts`. It has no lodash imports and no hand-written replacements, and the exported signatures are unchanged.

```ts
import { merge } from 'es-toolkit';
import { startCase } from 'es-toolkit/compat';
import { truncate } from 'es-toolkit/compat';
```

| Function | Replacement | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `applyPatch` | `merge` from `es-toolkit` | It mutates and returns the base object, merges arrays by index (`[1,2,3]` + `[9]` gives `[9,2,3]`), and handles null and type-changing patches. On my test inputs it matched the compat version, which is the lodash-compatible one. |
| `toTitle` | `startCase` from `es-toolkit/compat` | The strict `startCase` gives different results on consecutive capitals: `XMLHttp` becomes `Xml Http` instead of `XML Http`, and `ab12CD` becomes `Ab 12 Cd` instead of `Ab 12 CD`. Those inputs are in your range, so I used the compat version. |
| `preview` | `truncate` from `es-toolkit/compat` | `truncate` exists only in compat. |

- **Bundle size:** `npm run size -- out/module.ts` prints 2364 bytes (min+gzip) and 97 bytes of own code. Using the compat `merge` instead came to 4044 bytes, so I kept strict `merge`.
- **Type checking:** `tsc` reports errors only for `src/module.ts`, because lodash isn't installed. It reports none for `out/module.ts`.
- **Not run:** I couldn't compare against real lodash, since it isn't installed. The equivalence checks used `es-toolkit/compat` as the stand-in for lodash.
